heard: No human-made object had ever crossed the asteroid belt or reached Jupiter. In 1972, Pioneer 10 launched aboard an Atlas Centaur rocket, powered entirely by nuclear generators. It safely navigated the asteroid belt and flew within 82,000 miles of Jupiter in 1973. Intense Jovian radiation triggered false commands in the probe, yet it returned over 500 images. Its hull carried a gold plaque designed by Carl Sagan depicting two humans and 14 pulsars. In 1983, it passed Neptune's orbit, but navigators soon noticed a tiny, unexplained drift in its signal. This famous pioneer anomaly was eventually solved. The recoil of uneven heat radiation was gently tugging it. Silent since 2003, the spacecraft drifts toward the star Aldebaran after proving what deep space probes could survive.
